node-1.label: 17-year-old male presented with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions, with vesicles on trunk and upper extremities

node-2.label: Patient is a previously healthy 17-year-old male; one week prior he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved

node-3.label: He denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms; he had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before onset of the mucocutaneous eruption

node-4.label: Physical examination showed afebrile and no distress, normal vital signs including respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97%, shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate, circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis, 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities, with remainder of mucocutaneous, cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations unremarkable

why.why: Positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR, the mucocutaneous pattern, and both expert analyses converge on reactive mucocutaneous disease; no drug exposure and negative respiratory viral panel refute major alternative triggers. Confidence is raised from 0.80 to 0.85, tempered only by pending biopsy and autoimmune serologies.

Laboratory physician analysis explicitly favors viral exanthem with mucositis; positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR provides a direct viral trigger, and negative respiratory viral panel reduces alternative viral causes. Confidence is raised from 0.65 to 0.75, with confirmatory histopathology still pending.

New evidence of positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR provides a clear alternative viral etiology, and there was no drug exposure before onset. The patient is clinically stable without systemic toxicity, and the pathologist explicitly argues against drug-induced SJS/TEN. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.

The positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR shifts the etiology toward a viral reactive process, and no positive autoimmune findings have been identified. However, skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence and autoimmune blistering serologies are still pending, so immune-mediated mucocutaneous disorder cannot be completely excluded. Confidence is modestly lowered from 0.1 to 0.08.

node-1.label: 17-year-old male presented with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions, with vesicles on trunk and upper extremities

node-2.label: Patient is a previously healthy 17-year-old male; one week prior he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved

node-3.label: He denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms; he had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before onset of the mucocutaneous eruption

node-4.label: Physical examination showed afebrile and no distress, normal vital signs including respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97%, shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate, circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis, 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities, with remainder of mucocutaneous, cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations unremarkable

why.why: Positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR, the mucocutaneous pattern, and both expert analyses converge on reactive mucocutaneous disease; no drug exposure and negative respiratory viral panel refute major alternative triggers. Confidence is raised from 0.80 to 0.85, tempered only by pending biopsy and autoimmune serologies.

Laboratory physician analysis explicitly favors viral exanthem with mucositis; positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR provides a direct viral trigger, and negative respiratory viral panel reduces alternative viral causes. Confidence is raised from 0.65 to 0.75, with confirmatory histopathology still pending.

New evidence of positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR provides a clear alternative viral etiology, and there was no drug exposure before onset. The patient is clinically stable without systemic toxicity, and the pathologist explicitly argues against drug-induced SJS/TEN. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.02.

The positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR shifts the etiology toward a viral reactive process, and no positive autoimmune findings have been identified. However, skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence and autoimmune blistering serologies are still pending, so immune-mediated mucocutaneous disorder cannot be completely excluded. Confidence is modestly lowered from 0.1 to 0.08.
